messages:
maya: quick heads-up from canary: compact-slim q4 on staging has a small-but-noisy regression on mixed CJK + RTL locales. TL;DR: punctuation ordering flips and stray directional marks (U+200E/U+200F) appear in decodes for a subset of samples.
- fp32 BLEU: 29.7 chrF: 55.3
- q8 BLEU: 29.5 chrF: 55.0
- q4 BLEU: 25.9 chrF: 50.8 (mixed-orientation subset)
- affected samples show LRM/RLM inserted near bracket boundaries and parentheses mirrored on decode only in q4 canary

maya: tiny repro input I used: "(你好)     "
actual: (你好)  -> but real-case is mixing Arabic/Hebrew like: "(你好)    "
(example using visible placeholders: "(你好)   where placeholders map to RTL run)

maya: fp32 decode sample: "(你好)    \u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645 [世界]" (keeps order)
maya: q4 decode sample: ")你好( \u200F\u10 \u10 \u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645 ]世界[" (paren mirrored, U+200F inserted before Arabic run and before CJK bracket)

cheng: did the q4 package change any of the normalization or pre-tokenization steps? last time switching pre-normalize flag caused bidi artifacts. i'll diff tokenizer metadata and unicode lib versions. @li-wei can you dump tokens and visible codepoints for both fp32 and q4 runs?

li-wei: running token dumps now. quick snippet:
- fp32 token dump (token strings): ['(', '你好', ')', ' ', '\u2014', ' ', '\u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645', ' ', '[', '世界', ']']
- q4 token dump: ['(', '\u200E', '你好', ')', ' ', '\u2014', ' ', '\u200F', '\u0627\u0644\u0633\u0644\u0627\u0645', ' ', '[', '\u200E', '世界', ']']
(note: inserted LRMs/RLMs around locale boundaries in q4 runtime)

sahil: running q4 runtime with --no-compact-emit and --dump-tokens. preliminary: when compact-emit enabled the decode buffer includes literal directional bytes (0xE2 0x80 0x8E / 0xE2 0x80 0x8F) at chunk boundaries; the postprocess treats them as directional marks leading to visible U+200E/U+200F. with compact-emit disabled, tokens match fp32. i'll bisect the compact-emit changes.

eval-bot: CI check https://ci.redwood/run/9620 flagged regression on mixed-orientation/evalset-v5 (delta BLEU -3.8). attached samples: artifacts/9620/mixed-punct-jitter.jsonl

joan: saw a similar pattern on an earlier bringup where we accidentally allowed the runtime to inject LRM/RLM for internal cursor accounting and forgot to strip them before final postprocess. could be a kernel-level marker that should be invisible.

cheng: i diffed tokenizer.json between bundles: tokenizers version is same, but q4 bundle has pre-normalize=false. pushing a small branch force-nfkc-pre-tokenize to test if forcing NFKC before tokenization reduces the observed mirroring.

li-wei: validating both approaches: 1) force pre-NFKC on tokenization pipeline, 2) run with compact-emit disabled. quick local 100-sample run: pre-NFKC recovers ~1.6 BLEU of the drop; disabling compact-emit recovers ~3.2 BLEU. full mixed subset run queued. gist with dumps: https://gist.github.com/li-wei/mixed-punct-jitter-9620

sahil: bisect update: compact-emit commit d4f9 introduced a tiny write-marker used as chunk separator; when multibyte UTF-8 sequence lands on a boundary we end up writing marker bytes into output. fix will either ensure marker is not a valid UTF-8 sequence or we strip markers before postprocess. creating rollback patch for q4 canary until fix lands.

maya: action items: 1) @cheng test force-NFKC branch on full mixed subset, 2) @li-wei run the gist on staging with both fixes and attach results, 3) @sahil prepare emergency revert of compact-emit on q4 canary, 4) i'll open INF-1402 with linked CI artifacts and the gist. if tokenization-only helps we can gate pre-normalize by locale to avoid perf hit.

joan: small note: if we strip directional marks in postprocess as a short-term mitigation, be careful with intentionally inserted marks (some docs use LRM/RLM intentionally). prefer locale-based gating.

maya: thanks team. keep messages short here; i'll post the incident summary in INF-1402 once we confirm root cause and mitigation. :thumbsup:
